opening-quote.purpose: Atlas's line in the empty conversation: 26px/400, 20px on a phone; Arabic at 1.55 with no tracking.

headline.purpose: Each question at the top of its turn; dir=auto for Arabic.

title.purpose: Modal titles and headings inside an answer.

wordmark.purpose: "Atlas" beside the files-and-face mark in the top bar, neutral bright ink, Latin in both languages, the only 700 weight.

body.purpose: Answer prose (max 75ch) and composer text. Arabic interface text takes a 1.6 line height.

body-sm.purpose: Tree names, source rows, tables, trace, form labels, the opening's "— Atlas" (600), usage line.

label.purpose: Badges, source numbers, the Sources heading, sheet letters and row numbers; sentence case.

mono.purpose: SQL and tool input in the trace only.

shadows.name: xs / page
shadows.purpose: The rendered PDF page on the viewer stage.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Theme step; not used directly by app components.

shadows.name: md / overlay
shadows.purpose: Menus, popovers, comboboxes (model picker, voice picker).

shadows.name: lg / modal
shadows.purpose: Viewer and confirmation modals, over the overlay veil (32% graphite in light, 62% near-black in dark).

shadows.name: xl
shadows.purpose: Theme step; not used directly by app components.

shadows.name: float-edge (dark)
shadows.purpose: A shadow does not read on the near-black page, so modals take a hairline edge in dark and sit on the raised surface.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Theme motion token: finished parts fade and rise (4px turns, 2px tree rows), folder open and close, collapses, AppShell (the sidebar sliding, the sheet's 8px start margin) and modal transitions, trace chevron. AppShell drops it to zero while the sidebar edge is dragged.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Background, colour and border changes on rows, quiet controls and the composer focus border; the tree chevron turning; tooltips fade at 150ms; the sidebar edge line, 200ms after the pointer arrives.

motion.name: caret-pulse
motion.purpose: The streaming caret on the primary fill; static under reduced motion.

motion.name: avatar-loop
motion.value: requestAnimationFrame; pose eases with a 110ms half-life, the mouth with 45ms
motion.purpose: The bust only: in the call avatar while a call is open, and in the empty conversation, where it says its line and then waits (The Living Face Rule). Paused in a hidden tab; a still pose per state under reduced motion.

motion.name: avatar-blink
motion.value: 180ms (70ms close, 110ms open), every 2.8 to 6.5s, sometimes a quick second blink
motion.purpose: Call avatar blinks while its eyes are open.

motion.name: avatar-breath
motion.value: 4.2s sine, 0.7 units of rise in a 120-unit drawing
motion.purpose: Call avatar breath for the whole open call.

motion.name: avatar-ring-turn
motion.purpose: The dashed ring while the call connects and while a spoken question runs; no animation under reduced motion.

motion.name: opening-focus
motion.purpose: The bust comes into focus in the empty conversation once the tab is visible; eyes lowered, looking up at 380ms.

motion.name: opening-words
motion.value: 460ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) per word, 150ms apart from 760ms; 6px rise out of a 4px blur; mouth in 112ms syllables
motion.purpose: Atlas's line rising word by word as the bust says it.

motion.name: opening-byline
motion.purpose: "— Atlas" once the line is said.

motion.name: opening-composer-rise
motion.value: 560ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) transform from translateY(100%), 360ms ease-out opacity
motion.purpose: Once the line is said (or a click or key finishes it), the docked composer rises out of the sheet's foot; the column clips it so no scrollbar appears. About 1.6s in all. Only on a fresh page.

motion.name: opening-step-back
motion.value: 180ms out (opacity, 6px rise, 3px blur, then hidden), 320ms back, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: The face and its line step back while a question is in the box, a dictation runs or a call is open, and return when the box is empty, without saying the line again.

motion.name: opening-still
motion.value: none; a plain opacity fade when stepping back
motion.purpose: The opening under reduced motion: the still face, the whole line and the composer from the first frame, with no focus pull, rising words or rising box.

breakpoints.name: xs
breakpoints.purpose: Below it a source place always drops under its name; the call avatar drops to 56px with heavier lines, call controls grow to 40px, and only the latest caption shows; the opening bust drops to 120px and its line to 20px.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Below it the sidebar folds behind a burger in place of the sidebar toggle, its resize edge and the closed-sidebar sheet margin drop away, the sheet goes edge to edge with only its top hairline, language and theme move to the sidebar foot, Clear chat becomes an icon, the cost pair moves to the composer hint line, and the viewer goes full screen.

components.name: Opening
components.description: The empty conversation: the bust at 156px on the page ground comes into focus, looks up and says "Every answer, with its page." as the words rise one by one, then "— Atlas" while the composer rises out of the sheet's foot. It stays until a question is written. Any click or key finishes the line; reduced motion shows the still face, the whole line and the composer at once.
components.css: .ds-opening{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:24px;margin:0;padding:48px 16px;background:#fdfcfb;text-align:center;font-family:"Segoe UI", system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Helvetica Neue", "Noto Sans", "Noto Sans Arabic", "Geeza Pro", Tahoma, Arial, sans-serif}.ds-opening-face{display:block;width:156px;height:156px}.ds-opening-face .ring{fill:none;stroke:#dddcda;stroke-width:1px;vector-effect:non-scaling-stroke}.ds-opening-quote{max-inline-size:20ch;margin:0;color:#1b1917;font-size:26px;font-weight:400;line-height:1.3;letter-spacing:-0.01em;text-wrap:balance}.ds-opening-by{color:#696765;font-size:13px;font-weight:600}@media (max-width:36em){.ds-opening-face{width:120px;height:120px}.ds-opening-quote{font-size:20px}}

narrative.overview:
Atlas is the category standard for chat-with-your-documents tools, built to the craft of Claude.ai's calm reading column, Perplexity's numbered sources and Linear's dense, quiet chrome with the content on an inset sheet. The owner chose the conventions on purpose and the build doesn't dress them up. The palette is grounded in paper, pencil and a desk's manila folders: graphite and warm stone, with no blue cast. The 52px top bar and the sidebar (300px by default, dragged between 240 and 480px, or closed) are one continuous stone chrome field. The conversation sits on it as an inset sheet: the page ground, a 1px hairline and 8px corners, scrolling on its own while the chrome stays still. The sheet holds one 760px column. Everything is drawn with 1px hairlines on flat grounds. The one graphite appears only where the reader acts or where the system points at evidence.

The same world runs in two schemes and two languages. Dark is the same roles on warm graphite: the chrome darkest, the page a step up, raised surfaces a step above that. Every gray, ink, amber and red shade is a role, not a lightness step, and each role has its dark value, so a component that asks for "dimmed" or "red tint" reads correctly in both. The primary inverts by scheme: a graphite fill with white text in light, a chalk fill with graphite text in dark. Arabic mirrors the whole layout, while content (answers, questions, quotes, table cells, file names) keeps its own direction. Figures are Western digits in both languages, so a number on screen matches the number in the file.

Density follows Linear more than a marketing page. Tree rows are 13px names over 12px meta. Tables run at 13px with tabular figures. The answer reads at 15px with a 75ch measure. Motion only marks state changes: a hover tint, a chevron turning, a folder opening, the sidebar sliding, and the finished answer's table and sources settling in once with a short fade-and-rise. Two exceptions, both approved by the owner on 2026-10-29, and both are Atlas's face (a philosopher's bust in graphite line work, marble in both schemes): the opening of every fresh conversation, where the bust looks up, says its line and waits for the question, and a voice call, during which the face moves continuously.

The system refuses the demo look named in the direction contract: decorative gradients, glowing AI sparkles, bubble chat and cards inside cards. The question is a heading-weight line, not a bubble. The answer is plain prose on the page ground, not a card.
keyCharacteristics: One brand tone (graphite, a near-black at OKLCH hue 85 with almost no chroma, shade 7 of a 10-step ramp in both schemes; chalk in dark) for actions, focus, selection, links, citations, the open file, the streaming caret and the call avatar's ring while Atlas speaks
Warm stone neutrals in both schemes; nothing reads blue
One chrome field (top bar and sidebar) with the conversation on an inset sheet of page ground; the sidebar closes and resizes
Light and dark schemes from one set of colour roles; the PDF page and the bust stay white in both
File kinds wear the colour they are known by on their icons only: PDF red, Excel green, manila folders
1px hairline borders instead of shadows on every resting surface; floating surfaces also take a hairline edge in dark
One system UI family for everything (Segoe UI carries Arabic on Windows); monospace only for SQL and tool input
Tabular Western figures wherever numbers appear, in English and Arabic
The whole layout mirrors in Arabic; content keeps its own direction
Continuous motion lives only in the bust: in the empty conversation, and in the call avatar while a call is open

rules.name: The Graphite Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Graphite marks only what you can act on and where an answer points (primary action, focus, link, selection, active citation, cited text and cited rows, the open file, streaming caret, the sidebar edge while it moves, and the call avatar's ring while Atlas speaks). The wordmark and its mark, headings, icons and the drawing of the bust stay neutral.

rules.name: The Colour Means Trouble Rule
rules.body: Amber and red mean a file or request has a problem, nothing else. The one other use of colour is a file's kind, on its icon only: PDF red, Excel green, folders manila. A kind colour never reaches a name, a badge, a row ground or a notice. Document types and the ok state use neutral badges, empty and skipped files use gray, and "not found" answers use a neutral notice.

rules.name: The Roles Not Shades Rule
rules.body: A component asks for a role (gray 6 for dimmed, red 1 for the error tint, `--atlas-surface` for a raised surface, `--atlas-on-ink` for text on the primary, `--atlas-kind-pdf` for a PDF icon) and never for a lightness. The dark scheme gives every role its own value, so nothing is coloured per scheme in a component. The only fixed values are the ones that are real objects: the white PDF page and the marble bust.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every place a number appears sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Numeric table columns align right and never wrap.

rules.name: The Western Digits Rule
rules.body: Numbers are Western digits with comma thousands separators in both languages (counts, sizes, pages, amounts, times), the same as the documents and answers. Amounts are shown exactly as the data holds them, never rounded. Arabic counts use the noun's own plural form around the figure ("ملفان", "3 ملفات", "11 ملفًا").

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and badges are sentence case at zero tracking. The build has no uppercase or letterspaced text.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface that sits in the page gets a 1px border and no shadow. A shadow means the surface floats above the page, and in dark a floating surface also carries a hairline edge.

rules.name: The Fade Above The Dock Rule
rules.body: The one gradient in the system is functional: a 24px band above the docked composer that runs from transparent to the page ground, so turns scrolling under the composer fade out instead of being cut at its edge. It uses only the page ground, never a hue, and it is never decoration. No other surface takes a gradient.

rules.name: The Living Face Rule
rules.body: Continuous motion is allowed inside the bust only: in the empty conversation, where it says its line and then waits, and in the call avatar while a call is open. In a call it blinks every 2.8 to 6.5s, breathes on a slow 4.2s cycle, raises its brows while the user speaks, looks up while a question runs, moves its mouth with Atlas's measured voice, and its ring is dashed and turning while the call connects and while it checks. On the opening it comes into focus with its eyes lowered, looks up, and moves its mouth syllable by syllable with its line; then it blinks and glances now and then until a question is written. Under reduced motion it holds one still pose per state, and it does not move in a hidden tab. Every other surface keeps motion for state changes only.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius and shadow from the Mantine theme (`theme.ts`). Components carry no hex values.

Do ask for colour roles (gray 0 to 9, ink, yellow and red shades, `--atlas-surface`, `--atlas-focus`, `--atlas-on-ink`, `--atlas-kind-*`, `--atlas-folder-*`) so each surface reads in both schemes (The Roles Not Shades Rule).

Do keep graphite to actions, focus, selection, links, citations, cited rows, the open file, the streaming caret, the sidebar edge while it moves and the call avatar's speaking ring (The Graphite Is Evidence Rule).
Do put text on a primary fill in `--atlas-on-ink`, so it is white on graphite and graphite on chalk.
Do underline every link; graphite alone does not set a link apart from body text.
Do separate resting surfaces with 1px hairlines on chrome, page or surface grounds, and keep shadows for modals, menus and the PDF page; give floating surfaces a hairline edge in dark.
Do keep the conversation on the inset sheet, which scrolls on its own inside the still chrome field, and keep it off both window edges when the sidebar is closed.
Do make a hidden sidebar `inert`, and keep its width and open state for the next visit.
Do dock the question box at the sheet's foot from the start, with the page-ground fade above it, and let the opening hold the sheet until a question is written.
Do set every figure in tabular Western digits and right-align numeric columns physically, in both languages.
Do use logical properties so the whole layout mirrors in Arabic, `dir="auto"` on content, and isolates around file names, paths and codes inside Arabic sentences.
Do keep SQL, formulas, paths and the Excel grid left to right in both languages.
Do join an amount and its currency, and a number and its unit, with a no-break space.

Do use 150ms ease-out for hover and colour changes and 180ms `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for content settling in, collapsing, a folder opening or the sidebar sliding, and disable both under reduced motion.
Do use Tabler outline icons at 1.5 to 2 stroke, sized 12 to 18px. The manila folder glyph is the one authored icon.
Do give the bust a still pose per state under reduced motion, and stop its motion in a hidden tab (The Living Face Rule).
Do let any click or key finish the opening's line at once, and wait for the tab to be seen before it plays.
donts: Don't use decorative gradients, glowing AI sparkles, chat bubbles or cards inside cards. The page-ground fade above the docked composer is the only gradient (The Fade Above The Dock Rule).
Don't colour document types or ok files. Amber and red are for files and requests with problems only. A file's kind colour goes on its icon only, never on its name, badge, row or notice.
Don't put a shadow on a surface that sits in the page, including the inset sheet.
Don't pick a colour per scheme inside a component, or turn the PDF page or the bust dark.
Don't set uppercase or letterspaced labels. Labels are sentence case at 12px/600.
Don't add a second typeface or a display face. Monospace is for SQL and tool input only.
Don't use Eastern Arabic digits or round an amount for display.
Don't translate the wordmark, file names, item codes or numbers.

Don't choreograph page loads. The one exception, approved by the owner on 2026-10-29, is the opening of a fresh conversation, where the bust says its line and the composer rises; it plays on each load and each cleared chat, never blocks the app, and any click or key finishes it. Elsewhere motion marks state changes only, except inside the call avatar while a call is open.
Don't let a blue cast back into the neutrals or the brand tone. Grays and the dark ramp are warm stone; graphite has almost no chroma.
Don't colour the bust. Its drawing stays graphite on white marble in both schemes, and the brand tone touches only its ring while Atlas speaks.
